title: Negative: making the fuel, not the enzyme, limit the layered CIPS condensates (e0 0.18, kF 0.08) gives a frozen hexagonal lattice with no divisions and no deaths, not birth-death turnover
summary: Hypothesis: if the enzyme supply can fill the box with more bodies than the fuel can feed, divisions (driven by enzyme influx) and starvation deaths would keep alternating. Test: c40's layered dividing world (20261026T1100, unchanged code) with e0 0.18 (was 0.12) and kF 0.08 or 0.04 (was 0.2), 128x128, seed 0, t=15000. kF 0.08: 12 bodies nucleate at once by t~1300 into a near-hexagonal lattice and stay: 12 persistent tracks, 0 splits, 0 merges, 0 deaths (sheet, timeseries). kF 0.04: nothing nucleates. Fuel-limited bodies stop growing at the size their catchment feeds, the excess enzyme stays in the bath, and nothing pushes them to divide or die.

finding.operator: fuel-limited regime (high enzyme e0, low fuel regrowth kF)
finding.control: default e0 0.12, kF 0.2 (divides to 17-19 bodies, no deaths)
finding.result: e0 0.18/kF 0.08: 12 static bodies, 0 splits, 0 deaths in 15000 t; kF 0.04: no bodies

limits: One seed, 128x128, two parameter points; WORLD_P {"e0":0.18,"kF":0.08} and {"e0":0.18,"kF":0.04}. An intermediate regime with turnover may exist between these and the default.
